title: Family Digital Dossier
user: Adults who want a trusted family member or executor to locate essential digital records during illness or death without handing over their entire password vault today.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The asker worries that family would not know how to find banking, investments, wills, insurance, or documents; a commenter keeps an encrypted repository inventory in a separate secure location.
The emergency-access request describes a timeout-based trusted-contact flow for medical accidents or death and asks to limit access to selected sites.

recurrence: The need is triggered by life events but preparation is repeatedly deferred because existing password tools make it all-or-nothing and paperwork becomes stale.
current_workaround: Leave a paper notebook, share a master-password hint, maintain a private encrypted text file, or rely on a password manager's emergency feature alone.
incumbents_and_gap: Bitwarden, 1Password, and lawyers' estate plans address credentials or legal documents separately. The gap is a regularly reviewed locator dossier that records what exists and who to contact without storing secret credentials.
smallest_useful_product: An offline encrypted template that records institutions, document locations, renewal dates, emergency contacts, and executor instructions; it generates a review checklist and a printable sealed-cover sheet. Non-goals: password storage, legal advice, will generation, or automated account access.
success_measure: 60% of users complete at least ten locator entries and perform a scheduled six-month review; test recipients can locate three requested records using only the generated dossier.
monetization: one-time — a local continuity document should remain usable without a recurring account or vendor survival risk.
constraints: Client-side encryption with a clearly explained recovery model; collect no credentials by design; present jurisdiction-specific legal limitations prominently; users control print/storage security.
why_distinct: It fills the practical inventory-and-handoff gap around password managers instead of competing as one.
